relevance_note: Six identifiable patients with GAMT variants and GAMT deficiency are described individually in Table 1 ('of whom 6 were diagnosed with GAMT deficiency (CCDS2)').
method_note: Read the paper in full; a short Python script assembled the JSON from my reading, taking table cells programmatically from Table 1 and Table 2 rows for Patients 1-6 (checked against the tables by eye). Scope: of 14 CCDS patients, only Patients 1-6 (GAMT, CCDS2) are in scope; Patients 7-14 have SLC6A8 variants and get no rows. One further patient 'with variants in GAMT gene' excluded from CCDS by normal brain Cr on MRS is mentioned only as a count with no individual-level detail, so no row. Labels: Table 1 'Patients No.' column holds bare numbers, but the text uses 'Patient 1'...'Patient 6', so rule 1 applies. Patients 5 and 6 are stated to be brothers; no family label is given. Zygosity left 'not reported' for every variant: each patient row lists two GAMT variants but no zygosity; the only zygosity statement ('Seven patients with suspected CCDS had compound heterozygous variants in the GAMT gene') is a count of seven unnamed patients (six diagnosed plus the excluded one, presumably) and is not tied to named patients. 'Known'/'Novel' labels in Table 1 are novelty, not a pathogenicity class, so pathogenicity is 'not reported'. Parental samples were sequenced per Methods, but no per-patient parental result is given, so inheritance is 'not reported'. Normal MRI ('N', legend 'N, normal') for Patients 5 and 6 recorded as excluded 'abnormal brain MRI'; per D-27 this does not exclude the specific MRI checklist items, which stay not reported. Patient 2 GAA 2.84 has no arrow and lies within the printed reference range; no feature row was made for it (no explicit normal statement). Extracerebral space enlargement (Patient 2) and thin corpus callosum (Patient 3) are not mapped to checklist items. Group statements without names (age of onset 1-2 years for all; '9 had epilepsy'; '8 had movement or behavioral disorders') were not assigned to individuals. Ethnicity/country recorded as 'China' from the title (cohort study in China at a Chinese hospital); not stated per patient. Contradictions in the paper: cohort size 3,568 (Abstract) vs 3,586 (Introduction, Results); ornithine dose 400-500 mg/kg/day (Methods) vs 300-400 (Table 2); Patient 1 epilepsy resolved 'after 2 years' (Table 2) vs 'after 3-6 months' (Results); Patient 2 treatment duration '2 y 2 m' (Table 2) vs 'after 3 years of treatment' (Results); Discussion says Patients 2, 3 and 4 had epilepsy disappear, while Results names Patients 1, 3 and 4 and Table 2 says Patient 2 had 'Mild epilepsy that could be controlled'; Patients 5 and 6 treated '7 m'/'8 m' (Table 2) vs 'for 4 months' (Discussion); Discussion states c.403G>A in 5 patients and c.491dupG in 4 patients, but Table 1 shows each in only one patient (Patient 3 and Patient 1); Abstract says 6 novel variants, Conclusions 7; Results says 'GATM deficiency' where GAMT is meant. Treatment rows record outcomes as treatment detail only; post-treatment improvements were not made into excluded features. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper cites earlier Chinese GAMT reports by overlapping authors (refs 3, 42) but never states that any of its patients were described before.
